cleansingStrength.rationale: The formula is SLES-led and therefore clearly effective, but CAPB at position 3 plus early silicone/protein and later polymer/silicone care routes make ordinary balanced cleansing more likely than a strong reset label.
cleansingStrength.counterSignal: The anionic sulfate appears very early and there is no extra mild-anionic replacement for the primary cleansing role.

conditioningLevel.rationale: A substantial rinse-off conditioning effect is likely because dimethicone is unusually prominent and is joined by protein, amodimethicone, cationic guar and glycerin.
conditioningLevel.counterSignal: SLES/CAPB cleansing and rinse-off exposure prevent assuming leave-on repair or mask-level conditioning.

weightPotential.rationale: Noticeable loss of movement/root lift is plausible because an early dimethicone route is reinforced by amodimethicone, cationic guar and hydrogenated castor oil despite meaningful sulfate reset.
weightPotential.counterSignal: The same formula has a conventional SLES/CAPB cleansing base, so high is not based on ingredient count alone.

unresolvedFacts: PEG-120 METHYL GLUCOSE DIOLEATE at position 16 is unresolved only as a helper/thickener and is not counted as a substantive conditioning route.
weightAssessment.whyThisBand: The deposition system is not light: dimethicone appears at position 5, with amodimethicone and cationic guar later, making persistent coating plausible even in rinse-off use.
weightAssessment.whyNotNeighborBand: Not moderate because the early silicone position plus multiple reinforcing persistent routes exceed a bounded one-route residue signal; the SLES/CAPB base is a counterweight but does not erase deposition.

focusPrimary.rationale: The blind packet contains no product claim direction, so the provisional claim-gated focus remains general even though repair/care routes are formula-compatible.
focusPrimary.counterSignal: Protein and silicone routes make a later repair or shine focus plausible if supported by exact-product claims.

focusSecondary.rationale: No secondary focus is assigned in the blind pass because there is no distinct secondary positioning evidence.
focusSecondary.counterSignal: Separate protein and silicone/polymer routes could later support a distinct secondary focus if exact claims require it.

usageRole.rationale: Regular is the blind default because no allowed input contains a product-level usage trigger; strong cleansing alone would not be sufficient anyway.
usageRole.counterSignal: The formula has a rich care system that could affect practical cadence, but usage role is product-level and claim-triggered.

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: No recognized scalp actives or sensitive/comfort intent are visible, and fragrance exposure occurs early enough to be a comfort counter-signal.
scalpComfortTarget.counterSignal: Glycerin and buffered cleansing are comfort-compatible but do not establish targeted scalp-comfort positioning by themselves.

dandruffSupport.rationale: The complete formula contains neither Piroctone Olamine nor Climbazole.
dandruffSupport.counterSignal: SODIUM SALICYLATE at position 26 does not qualify under the exact mechanical rule.
